title: Predictive Headroom Scheduler for Dedicated Fleets
author: Ava Martinez
description: Introduce a predictive headroom scheduler that reserves and releases dedicated fleet capacity based on short-term traffic forecasts and tenant-level SLO intents. Motivation: current reactive autoscalers oscillate under bursty traffic and either overprovision (wasting committed capacity) or underprovision (breaching throughput SLAs). This PR implements an EWMA-based short window predictor augmented with anomaly suppression, a configurable confidence margin, and soft caps for burst-bank integration so tenants keep predictable burst behavior while preserving long-term utilization. Key user-visible behavior: new fleet config fields (prediction_window_seconds, confidence_margin_pct, warmup_duration_seconds, anomaly_backoff) and a per-tenant score that maps predicted QPS to an allocation delta. The scheduler integrates with existing burst token pool logic but prefers predictive headroom for gradual scale-up and falls back to immediate burst tokens only when prediction error is high. Also adds telemetry: predicted_vs_actual_qps histogram, headroom_reservations_gauge, and prediction_error_rate alert. Implementation notes: scheduler service running as part of fleet-controller selects scale actions every 5s by default; uses historical 60s sliding window for EWMA with optional ARIMA feature-flag for customers who opt in on Dedicated. The rollout is gated: config flag predictive_headroom.enabled default false; rollout plan includes Canary on two low-risk fleets, blue/green for Dedicated control plane, and a kill-switch that reverts to legacy autoscaler if error_rate > 5% for 10m. Includes unit and integration tests, new e2e perf canary scenario, and operator docs for tuning margins and warmup. Backwards compatibility: existing autoscaler configs remain valid; predictive configs are additive. See Linear ENG-6291 for acceptance criteria and metrics targets.

merge_commit_message:
squash: predictive headroom scheduler for dedicated fleets

Adds EWMA predictor, integration with burst bank, telemetry, tests, and operator docs. Gates via feature flag.
merge_outcome_notes: Merged after canary validation; no rollback needed. Enabled behind feature flag; dedicated customers must opt in. Canary showed 12% reduction in short-term overprovisioning on test fleets and maintained 99.9% throughput SLO during burst windows.
release_notes: Introduce predictive headroom scheduler for Dedicated fleets (opt-in). Improves short-term provisioning accuracy to reduce wasted reserved capacity and maintains burst guarantees. Operator tuning guide added.
